For now the block sits at the top | | `p {` | The **selector**: which tag the rule is for | It names a kind of tag, so every `

` changes, not just the first. The `{` opens the rule | | `color: teal;` | A **property**, a colon, a **value** and a semicolon | `color` is the text colour. Colours can be names such as `teal`, `navy` or `crimson`. The `;` ends the line | | `font-size: 28px;` | Sets how big the text is | `px` is the unit. Other properties: `font-family: sans-serif;`, `background-color: lightyellow;`, `text-align: center;` | | `}` | Closes the rule | A rule can hold as many property lines as you like | | the `

` and `

` lines | Stay as they were | The rule names `p` only, and the HTML did not change | ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#third insight: "A rule names a kind of tag and changes every tag of that kind; it changes how it looks, never what it is." tasks: - check: type: trace text: "A third paragraph is added to the page. Fill in the colour of each line of text." table: | | text | tag | colour | | Sports day | h1 | black | | Sports day is on Friday. | p | teal | | What to bring | h2 | [black] | | Bring a hat and water. | p | [teal] | | Races start at 9 am. | p | [teal] | fault: logic misconception: rule-styles-one explain: "The rule picks every p, including one added later, so all three paragraphs are teal. The h1 and h2 are different tags, so the rule leaves them alone." - check: type: question code: page.html#small q: "The rule h1 { font-size: 14px; } makes the heading smaller than the paragraphs. Is it still a heading?" options: - "Yes: the

tag still says it is the main heading; the rule changed only how it looks" - "No: it is just small text now" - "No: a heading has to be the biggest text on the page" - "Yes, but only until the page is saved" answer: 0 fault: logic misconception: looks-is-structure explain: "The tag says what a part is, and the rule says how it looks. Making an

small does not turn it into a paragraph, and screen readers and search engines still treat it as the main heading." ``` ### Three paragraphs A new paragraph appears at the end of the page. Which lines does the rule colour? ### Small but still a heading Look at the rule for `h1`. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Writing rules one at a time: change a value, add a property, add a rule for another tag." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#modify", height: 440 } tasks: - hint: "Change only the value after color:, and keep the semicolon." check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed the heading's colour." } expected: page.html#sol-colour - hint: - "Add a new rule inside the `." - see: Only the first property in a rule works. ask: Does every property line end with a semicolon? fix: "Add the missing ; after the value, as in color: teal;" - see: The CSS shows on the page as text. ask: Is the CSS inside ? fix: Put every rule between at the top of the page. stretch: "Try font-size: 12px on the h1 and 60px on the p. Then ask whether the h1 is still a heading, and how a screen reader would know." support: "Give students the Modify starter and do the second task together on the board: the selector, the braces, then one property line." leads: "Next lesson is lists: a rule for li styles every item at once. Later, classes let you pick only some tags of a kind. Class idea: restyle the same page three ways (calm, loud, sporty) without changing the HTML." exit: q: "A rule h2 { color: purple; } is added to a page with four h2 headings. How many turn purple, and is any

changed into something else?" a: "All four turn purple, because the selector names the tag. None changes into something else: the tag is still h2, and the rule only changes how it looks." explain: | The video and the picture show the same steps: 1. CSS rules go in a `
